business_scope.primary_industry_name: Die-Struck Brass Cloisonné Polishing of Novelty Enamel Badges

meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: France (single national jurisdiction; unitary state with no sub-state tax distinction for SARL purposes)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Convention between the Government of the French Republic and the Government of the People's Republic of China for the Avoidance of Double Taxation with respect to Taxes on Income and Capital (signed 26 November 2013; in force from 1 January 2015)

Agreement between the Government of the French Republic and the Government of the People's Republic of China on the Reciprocal Encouragement and Protection of Investments (signed 30 May 1984; in force)
EU-China Comprehensive Agreement on Investment (negotiated 2020; pending ratification and therefore not yet active)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Code monétaire et financier (CMF) Article L.561-2-2 and Articles L.561-1 to L.561-57, with implementing Articles R.561-1 to R.561-70, as amended by Ordinance No. 2020-115 of 12 February 2020 transposing Directive (EU) 2018/843; Decree No. 2018-284 of 18 April 2018 on AML/CFT obligations; UBO register (Registre des bénéficiaires effectifs - RBE) introduced by Law No. 2016-731 of 3 June 2016 (Sapin II); UBO filing obligation enforced through the INPI Guichet unique at incorporation; AML/CFT supervision by the ACPR and the TRACFIN financial intelligence unit.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation / Business License of the foreign corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) of the People's Republic of China
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille of a notarized copy issued by the Chinese Ministry of Foreign Affairs or authorized Provincial Foreign Affairs Office (China party to the Hague Convention since 7 November 2023)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing / Active Status of the foreign corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille via Chinese MFA or authorized Provincial Foreign Affairs Office

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution and Power of Attorney authorizing incorporation of the French SARL and appointment of the Gérant
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent corporate body of the foreign shareholder; Chinese notary public
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Chinese notarization followed by Hague Apostille

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Passport copies and identity documentation of the ultimate beneficial owner and the appointed Gérant
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Chinese notarization + Hague Apostille, thereafter certified French translation by a court-registered sworn translator (traducteur assermenté)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of each 25% and above UBO plus the Gérant against the UN Security Council consolidated sanctions list, the EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List (EEAS), Council Regulation (EU) No. 269/2014 and Council Regulation (EU) No. 833/2014 as amended, French domestic asset-freeze orders (arrêtés de gel des avoirs issued by the Ministry of Economy, DG Trésor), and the US OFAC SDN list whenever any transaction touches USD clearing. PEP screening is mandatory under FATF Recommendation 12 and CMF Articles L.561-10 and L.561-10-2, covering domestic and foreign politically exposed persons, family members and close associates. All screening evidence must be recorded in a KYC/AML file retained for at least five (5) years after termination of the business relationship.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Guichet unique des formalités des entreprises operated by the INPI - https://formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr (interfaced with the Registre National du Commerce et des Sociétés and the Infogreffe database)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Mandatory French language for the corporate name, articles of association and all filed documents under Law No. 94-665 of 4 August 1994 (Toubon Law). The company name must be expressed in Latin script with French diacritics; a non-French denomination such as Chinese pinyin is accepted only in phonetically transliterated Latin characters and is prohibited where it misleads as to nationality, public body, regulated activity or public order. The letters 'SARL' or the full expression 'Société à responsabilité limitée' must accompany the company name in all commercial and statutory documents, together with the registered share capital figure.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: banque / établissement de crédit / société de financement (prior ACPR authorization mandatory)
assurance / société d'assurance / mutuelle / institution de prévoyance (regulatory authorization mandatory)
avocat / notaire / commissaire de justice / expert-comptable / commissaire aux comptes (reserved regulated professions)
société de gestion de portefeuille (prior AMF authorization mandatory)
France / République / État / national / officiel (misleading public connotation prohibited)
SA / SAS / EURL or any alternative legal-form token causing confusion with the SARL form
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: France does not operate a common-law style statutory name reservation; the name is verified and inscribed at the moment of incorporation filing. The 30-day window reflects the recommended validity period for the notarized and apostilled foreign documentation bundle used as name-clearance evidence. Upon a reasoned refusal by the INPI/greffier, Step 1: file a rectification application (complément) through the Guichet unique with legal argumentation demonstrating absence of identity or confusing similarity with existing RCS entries, absence of infringement of earlier trademark rights verified through the INPI trademark database, and full public-order conformity. Step 2: if refused again, lodge a judicial appeal against the registry officer's decision before the President of the competent Tribunal judiciaire (commercial division) in summary proceedings (référé) within one (1) month from notification, pursuant to the Code de commerce procedures governing registry refusals. Step 3 (commercial expedient): adopt an alternative approved name by a shareholders' decision while refiling the first-choice name as an INPI trademark application to secure a seniority right.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Statutorily permitted for the administrative registered office (siège social) only through a licensed commercial domiciliation provider (domiciliataire agréé) or an approved business incubator under the French domiciliation regime. A pure virtual office lacking a physical set of premises, a licensed domiciliation contract and mail-receiving capacity is not recognized by the registry. For hard enamel lapel pin manufacturing, the production plant must be separately declared as an établissement with its own SIRET registration in addition to the domiciled siège social.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Approximately 15% cumulative probability within the first 24 months for a low-risk manufacturing SARL; the risk is driven by mixed compliance supervision by URSSAF, DGFiP, DGCCRF and French Customs (DGDDI), all entitled to perform unannounced on-site inspections.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Drafting of SARL articles of association (statuts) by a licensed French avocat including structural review of capital, ownership and management clauses
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Avocat inscrit au barreau (recommended: Barreau de Paris)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for a standard multi-member SARL; typical flat fee range USD 2,000-3,500

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Company incorporation filing through the INPI Guichet unique (immatriculation au Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés including issuance of the Kbis excerpt)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Institut National de la Propriété Industrielle (INPI)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory official tariff of the INPI fee schedule (approximately EUR 24 with minor annual indexation)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Mandatory publication of the incorporation legal notice in an authorized legal announcements gazette (Journal d'annonces légales)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Journal d'annonces légales authorized by the Préfecture of the registered-office department
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Authorized gazette tariff; commonly EUR 130-180 per publication depending on drafting complexity

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Preparation and filing of the UBO declaration (déclaration de bénéficiaire effectif) as part of the RCS registration dossier (RBE)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: INPI / Greffe RCS via the Guichet unique; drafting assistance provided by the avocat
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Filing right absorbed in the registration tariff; auxiliary compliance drafting at prevailing market benchmark for a single-tier ownership chain

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarization and Hague Apostille of the Chinese corporate shareholder dossier (business license, good standing letter, board resolution and UBO passports)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Chinese notary office and Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the People's Republic of China or authorized Provincial Foreign Affairs Office
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing PRC notarial and apostille documentary scale; aggregate estimate for the four-document bundle

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Court-certified sworn French translation (traduction assermentée) of corporate, statutory and UBO identification documents
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Traducteur assermenté registered with the Court of Appeal as judicial expert
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: French court-official tariff per page; market benchmark for a 10-14-page bundle

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Licensed commercial domiciliation of the registered office — 12-month initial contract
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for Paris region; annual EUR 240-600 invoiced for the first year at formation

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Opening of the French professional bank account (temporary blocked account for share capital movement and subsequent operational flows) including AML/CFT enhanced due diligence
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: French credit institution (e.g. BNP Paribas, Crédit Agricole, Société Générale or eligible neo-bank)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark for account-opening package; activation, overdraft and monthly maintenance charges invoiced separately after incorporation

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: EORI number registration with French Customs (DGDDI) and VAT identification (immatriculation TVA) application
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Direction Générale des Douanes et Droits Indirects (DGDDI) / Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutorily free of charge; no filing duty collected by the French State

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Code de commerce (France), Livre II — Book II on Commercial Companies: Articles L.223-1 to L.223-43 (Société à Responsabilité Limitée — formation, capital, governance); Articles L.210-1 to L.210-10 (registration with the RCS, effects of the Kbis); Décret n° 2023-700 (Guichet unique — unified electronic formalities); Code de l'environnement Article R.122-2 for environmental screening thresholds.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) held by the Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce du lieu du siège social; electronic filing processed through the Institut National de la Propriété Industrielle (INPI) Guichet Unique at formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Déclaration M0 — formulaire de création d'entreprise (electronic M0 data set) filed via the INPI Guichet Unique; the resulting proof of incorporation is the official 'Extrait Kbis' issued by the competent Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No de jure minimum share capital for an SARL (freedom of capital under Article L.223-2, Code de commerce); the capital must be fully subscribed and cash contributions fully paid up at formation, deposited in a blocked escrow account held by a French bank, the Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations, or a notaire (Article L.223-7); the bank's 'attestation de dépôt des fonds' must accompany the M0 filing, and funds are released upon issuance of the Kbis.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: UNANIMOUS WRITTEN CONSENT OF THE PARTNERS OF [•] SARL — FIRST RESOLUTION. The partners: (i) approve the final Articles of Association; (ii) subscribe and allocate the entire share capital of EUR [•], acknowledging full payment into the blocked escrow account; (iii) adopt the registered office at [address]; (iv) appoint [name] as Gérant for an indefinite term with full management powers, noting no regulated activity; and (v) authorize the Gérant to file the formation dossier on the INPI Guichet Unique, publish the legal notice, open bank accounts, and obtain the Kbis extract. This consent is recorded in the annex to the minutes.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of Articles of Association and Appointment of the Gérant
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: All founding partners (associés); a notaire (notary) is optional when no real-property contribution is made; beneficial-owner screening via the INPI/Infogreffe prior checks.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the statuts (private deed or notarial deed) under Articles L.223-1 to L.223-6; insert the corporate object covering die-struck brass novelty enamel badges and merchandise, the registered office address, share capital, description of each partner's contribution, and the appointment of the Gérant. Each partner signs the statuts and the First Resolution; the Gérant signs the customary declaration of non-conviction; assemble the beneficial-owner declaration (DBE). No legalization or apostille is required for domestic filing, but certified copies must be uploaded in PDF where requested.
required_dossiers: Signed Articles of Association (statuts) with annexes
Identity documents of each partner (passport or national ID)
Bank RIB of the company if a pre-registration account was opened
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Greffe queries any statutory clause, cure by executing a supplementary deed (avenant) or a new unanimous resolution before submission of the M0; no registration fee is forfeited until the formal filing is transmitted.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Escrow Deposit of Share Capital in a Blocked Bank Account
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Authorized French credit institution, the Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations, or a notaire acting as depositary.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a temporary account under the corporate name 'SARL [•] en formation'; each partner wires the amount of his or her cash contribution; the bank verifies source of funds under AML/KYC rules and issues the 'attestation de dépôt des fonds' confirming the total amount and the blocked nature of the funds until the RCS registration is effective; obtain the bank certificate and hold it for the M0 filing; unblock the funds upon presentation of the first Kbis.
required_dossiers: Identity documents of all partners and of the Gérant
Bank KYC/AML questionnaire and source-of-funds evidence
Account opening application signed by the designated signatories
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a commercial bank refuses the deposit for internal KYC reasons, use the Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations or a notaire as statutory depositary; ensure the name on the attestation matches the exact corporate name intended for the RCS.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publication of the Mandatory Legal Notice (Annonce Légale)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: A legal gazette (Journal d'Annonces Légales) approved by the Préfecture of the département where the registered office is located.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the legal notice content to the approved gazette: corporate name, legal form (SARL), share capital, registered office, corporate object, Gérant, RCS city, and duration. Pay the gazette's regulated publication fee (approximately EUR 190, varying by department); obtain the publisher's 'attestation de parution' certifying the effective publication date; retain the attestation for attachment to the M0 filing.
required_dossiers: Extract of the signed Articles of Association
Payment receipt for the publication fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If publication is delayed, select another approved gazette in the same department; if the notice contains a material error (name, capital, misstatement of object), publish a corrective rectification notice and obtain a corrected attestation before filing the M0.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP) — Portal: impots.gouv.fr; online company formalities: formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Incorporate the SARL via the French 'Guichet unique' formalities portal to obtain SIREN/SIRET; the DGFiP automatically opens the corporate tax file and allocates the TVA intracommunautaire number (FR + 2-digit key + SIREN). Foreign entities without a French establishment must apply for direct French VAT registration through the SIE (Service des Impôts des Entreprises) and file under the non-resident taxpayer procedure.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation — the SARL is taxable at entity level under Impôt sur les Sociétés (25% standard, 15% reduced rate on profits up to EUR 42,500) on worldwide profits, with territoriality adjustments for foreign permanent establishments; no automatic pass-through status exists.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box regime. A qualifying 'family SARL' may elect income tax (IR) treatment under CGI Art. 239 bis AA for a renewable 5-year term; hybrid mismatch anti-avoidance rules under CGI Art. 212 bis (ATAD) restrict deductions in EU/non-EU mismatched arrangements.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (Taxe sur la Valeur Ajoutée — TVA)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EUR 91,900 annual turnover for goods sales (franchise en base, CGI Art. 293 B); EUR 36,800 for services; EU-wide distance-selling threshold of EUR 10,000 applies for OSS registration on cross-border B2C supplies.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Phased e-invoicing and e-reporting under CGI Art. 289 bis: mandatory from 1 September 2026 for large and mid-sized companies and from 1 September 2027 for SMEs; B2B invoices must be exchanged through DGFiP-certified PDP platforms and transaction data transmitted to the Portail Public de Facturation. No national real-time pre-clearance stamping; periodic quasi-real-time reporting applies.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of goods dispatched outside the EU qualify for 0% VAT exemption under CGI Art. 262-I-1 provided title and risk have passed to the non-EU buyer and physical export is evidenced within the prescribed documentation window; intra-EU B2B supplies are exempt under CGI Art. 262 ter I with a valid EU customer VAT number; export-related ancillary services may also be zero-rated under strict conditions.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Export customs declaration (DAU / DELTA electronic lodgement clearing the goods to exit the EU)
Commercial invoice showing HS 8306/7117 classification, EXW/FOB value, and INCOTERM
Bill of Lading, CMR, or Air Waybill evidencing physical departure from EU territory
Inward payment proof (SWIFT MT103 credit advice or Stripe/Etsy payout reports) establishing inward remittance
CARNET/transit documentation when goods transit through non-EU or bonded regimes
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: VAT authorities may claw back zero-rated benefits where export evidence is not retained for six years; CGI Art. 283-3 reversal applies with monthly late-payment interest of 0.40% (Art. 1727), a 40% bad-faith penalty, or 80% penalty for concealed activity (Arts. 1730/1731); customs fines under Code des douanes Art. 413 can reach the value of the goods; export receivables outstanding beyond 180 days trigger transfer-pricing and hidden-distribution recharacterization under CGI Art. 57.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque de France (BdF) and Autorité de Contrôle Prudentiel et de Résolution (ACPR), acting within the Single Supervisory Mechanism of the European Central Bank; foreign-exchange policy competence is shared with the Direction Générale du Trésor (French Treasury, Ministère de l'Économie et des Finances). For payment statistics, foreign-exchange control reports and statutory intermediary oversight, Banque de France is the designated authority under the Code Monétaire et Financier (CMF).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: France confirms full euro convertibility on both current and capital account; French exchange controls have been fully dismantled, and no convertibility restriction applies to legitimate commercial or treasury transactions. Capital movements with non-EU countries are free under TFEU Article 63; ISIC 3240 die-struck brass enamel-pin production is outside the foreign-investment screening sectors of décret n° 2018-1291 (defence, dual-use, critical infrastructure, cybersecurity, etc.), so no ex-ante FDI authorisation applies. Profit remittance to non-resident shareholders is unrestricted and taxed only via withholding (default 30% under French law when paid to non-residents, reduced by applicable double-tax treaties). The SARL must comply with Banque de France statistical reporting: any single transfer of €12,500 or more must be routed through an authorised intermediary, and cumulative inbound FDI exposure above €1.5 million requires an annual BdF balance-of-payments return. No stabilisation levy, surrender quota or convertibility charge is imposed.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: France imposes no statutory obligation to surrender, repatriate or convert export proceeds. Exporters may freely receive revenue in EUR, USD, GBP, JPY, CNY or any convertible currency, hold foreign-currency accounts and convert at authorised bank market rates. For compliance routing, all cross-border settlements of €12,500 or more must be transacted through a French or EU-passported authorised intermediary (l'intermédiaire agréé) and declared to Banque de France for balance-of-payments statistics. Marketplace proceeds aggregated by Etsy Direct Pay or Stripe are not exempt from these pass-through reporting duties; where the payment institution (e.g., Stripe Payments Europe Ltd) is itself the intermediary, its statutory reporting covers the underlying transactions. Finished goods exported directly from French customs to consumers require CN22/CN23 declarations on the postal/courier side and French export statistics (DEB/DAU) above the statistical threshold, but no foreign-exchange surrender ratio is applicable.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Compte Professionnel (Operational Account) + Compte de Dépôt des Fonds (Capital Escrow Account during incorporation)
Compte Courant Professionnel (Operational Account) with dedicated Export and FX Desk

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Crédit Agricole – LCL (Le Crédit Lyonnais SA)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Compte Professionnel (Operational Account); capital deposit escrow available

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Crédit Mutuel / CIC (Crédit Industriel et Commercial SA)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Compte Professionnel (Operational Account) for SMEs; import/export settlement desk available

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: EU/EEA-authorised electronic money institutions (Qonto SA via ACPR licence; Treezor SA; Revolut Ltd via Lithuanian EMI passport; and similar DSP2-passported issuers) may lawfully provide payment accounts to the FR_SARL and are viable as primary or ancillary liquidity rails. Viability rating: High for EU-licensed EMIs. Non-EU or offshore EMIs (UK post-Brexit payment institutions without French/EU passporting, US payment facilitators, Caribbean or Asian EMIs lacking a French/EU authorisation) are legally acceptable only as technical settlement sub-layers: the actual outward cross-border payment must be cleared through an EU authorised intermediary, and an offshore EMI cannot replace or obfuscate that statutory routing. Sole reliance on a non-passported offshore EMI is rated Low; use as an embedded acceptance or expense-card layer above a mainstream French bank is rated Medium/Low due to enhanced ACPR scrutiny of chained disbursements from France.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: For a domestically incorporated SARL, remote opening is technically permitted under CMF Article L561-5 where identity verification occurs via a secure video KYC process consistent with ACPR instructions. In practice, first-tier French banks generally require a physical interview with the statutory gérant, or at minimum a live video interview, where any beneficial owner is a non-resident individual. Remote onboarding is realistic when: (i) the gérant holds an EU passport or residence permit; (ii) notarised/apostilled corporate documents are furnished; (iii) certified copies of identification and source-of-funds evidence are provided; and (iv) the SARL's SIREN/VAT registration is verified. For this FR_SARL profile, the acceptable execution route is a physical meeting with the manager at the chosen branch (or video KYC at BNP Paribas or Société Générale where identification documents are EU-passported), plus presentation of the constitutional deposit certificate and completion of the statutory AML questionnaire (fiche de renseignements).

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-EU resident individual or corporate Ultimate Beneficial Owner (UBO) identified at a level of 25% or more; the bank escalates to enhanced due diligence (EDD) under CMF Article L561-10.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Deliver (1) sworn UBO declaration filed at the Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés; (2) identity verification of each UBO via apostilled/legalised passport copies with face-match; (3) tax residency certificate from the UBO's jurisdiction; (4) source-of-wealth and source-of-funds report supported by 12 months of personal bank statements and asset-title evidence; (5) corporate register extract where a UBO is itself a corporate entity; (6) legal opinion confirming that the capital is not of illicit provenance and that the transaction has no nexus to corruption or tax evasion, prepared in line with ACPR Annex II guidelines.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Initial capital deposit for constitution (statutory minimum is de minimis, but relevant practice is €1,000–€20,000 deposited in the escrow account) triggers CMF Article L561-5 origin-of-funds checks.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: (1) Certified copy of the shareholders' funding agreement; (2) bank statements of each contributing shareholder evidencing a 3-6 month fund pedigree; (3) if financed by shareholder loan, a loan deed with business-plan justification and repayment schedule; (4) certificate of deposit (attestation de dépôt des fonds) issued by the depositary institution; (5) certified accountant's statement confirming that the funds correspond to the capital clause in the Articles of Association.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Daily incoming payments from e-commerce marketplaces (Etsy Direct Pay, Stripe) reflecting aggregated consumer payouts in USD/GBP/EUR may be profiled as high-volume third-party or payment-intermediary activity, requiring proof that business revenues match settlement patterns.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: (1) Marketplace account documentation proving business verification (Etsy Seller ID and SARL registration match); (2) six months of settlement reports mapped to invoice lines and shipment identifiers (CN22/CN23 customs forms, courier tracking numbers); (3) French customs export declarations and EU VAT returns (CA3) showing alignment; (4) unit-price justification via bill of materials and component purchase invoices from brass/enamel suppliers; (5) a documented treasury policy explaining daily sweeps from Stripe/Etsy to the main operational account with no handling of third-party funds; (6) the payment processor's own AML/KYC status (Stripe Payments Europe Ltd authorised via Central Bank of Ireland ACPR passport, and Etsy Payments Ireland Ltd).

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Payments to Asian subcontractors (China/Taiwan-based polishing and moulding vendors for die-struck brass) attract sanctions/embargo and trade-transaction screening under EU Regulation 833/2014 and French customs oversight.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: (1) Signed purchase orders, pro-forma invoices and LC/SWIFT contracts identifying each counterparty's corporate UBO; (2) sanctions screening log evidencing negative hits on EU/UN/OFAC/Banque de France lists, dated and signed by the compliance officer; (3) compliance attestations accompanied by certificates of origin for raw materials; (4) end-use statements confirming shipments are consumer accessories (enamel lapel pins, ISIC 3240 class); (5) the bank's correspondent-banking due-diligence output (KYC/OFAC check) appended to the commercial file.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Equity injections and shareholder-loan disbursements to the FR_SARL must be paid in EUR to the operational account through an authorised intermediary (the French bank or an EU/EEA bank passporting into France). Standard routing: SEPA Credit Transfer (IBAN FR76-...) for EUR, or SWIFT MT103 for non-EUR currencies; the transfer's purpose code must align with Banque de France statistical categories — '201'/inward direct investment (IDE) where share capital is increased, and 'credit financier' category for shareholder current-account advances. For all inward transfers of €12,500 or more, the deposit-holding intermediary reports under CMF Article R152-1 and must secure an FDI identification workflow when cumulative injected stock crosses the €1.5 million threshold (annual BdF IDE return). Since EUR is a reserve currency and France is an IMF Article VIII member, no IMF or dual-currency approval is required; verification comprises the shareholder resolution, deposit certificate, and a balance sheet updated to the value date of injection.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Trade-payable settlements (brass sheet, copper-alloy blanks, enamel pigments, moulding tooling, subcontract polishing) are executed via SWIFT MT103 direct payments to the vendor's account; each message must quote the invoice number, HS codes for the underlying goods, and the final-beneficiary account details. For established relationships, commercial documentary credits under UCP600 remain permissible where foreign suppliers require bank confirmation; EU suppliers may alternatively be paid by SEPA Credit Transfer. The bank's international desk performs EUR-to-CNY and EUR-to-USD conversion at the same-day fixing using the MT103's settlement currency; no additional French Treasury declaration is required at transaction level because the intermediary files the Banque de France balance-of-payments return. Recurring orders below €12,500 may be routed by express SWIFT or SEPA, but sanctions and beneficiary screening applies to every payment.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: EUR/USD deliverable forward (FXA) with any French or EU authorised credit institution, OTC, bilateral or cleared, tenors 1M–12M
EUR/GBP deliverable forward for conversion of Etsy UK and UK-consumer GBP settlement balances
EUR/JPY deliverable forward for Japan-focused direct-to-consumer receipts
EUR/CNY non-deliverable forward (NDF) permitted where CNY convertibility is limited onshore; execution exclusively through a licensed EU bank desk with supporting trade documentation
FX swap (FXS) allowed for short-term EUR/USD rolling to cover working-capital ladder

Cross-currency interest-rate swap (CCIRS) permissible under EMIR where clearing thresholds are not triggered; for a small exporting SARL, plain-vanilla outright forwards and zero-cost collar structures are the recommended instruments

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual ordinary general meeting (AGO) approving the annual accounts and management report
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registered office – corporate book of minutes; no external filing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Held within six months of the financial year close, unless extended by court order
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Civil liability of the manager; court-ordered convocation upon shareholder application; risk of nullification of resolutions if statutory formalities omitted.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Filing of approved annual accounts (dépôt des comptes annuels) with the trade registry
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month after shareholder approval; approval itself must occur within six months of the financial year close
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative penalty up to EUR 3,000 for a legal entity; automatic denial of Kbis issuance until filed; formal notice may lead to strike-off from the trade and companies register.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporation tax return (liasse fiscale): Form No. 2065-SD with schedules 2050 series
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP) – Service des Impôts des Entreprises
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For calendar-year closings: no later than 30 April of the following year; for other year-ends: within three months of the financial year close
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of 5% of tax due plus 0.2% monthly interest; 10% surcharge after a 30-day formal notice; penalties rise to 40% for bad faith and 80% for fraudulent non-filing, subject to a minimum EUR 150 fine.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Balance payment of corporate income tax (solde d'IS) due with the annual return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Payable by the same deadline as the annual corporation tax return; for calendar-year closings the practical payment cutoff is usually 15 May
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Immediate 5% late-payment surcharge plus 0.2% monthly late-payment interest; enforced recovery by garnishment and property seizure after formal notice.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual audit and update of statutory registers and share-transfer records
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registered office – internal statutory records; presented to auditors, shareholders, tax inspectors, and registry upon request
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Completed no later than the annual shareholders' meeting; no external filing deadline
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Defective or falsified records may invalidate share transfers as against third parties, cause management civil liability, and create criminal exposure for forgery or fraud.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A statutory auditor (commissaire aux comptes) is required for an SARL when, at the close of two consecutive financial years, the company exceeds two of the following three thresholds: total balance-sheet assets exceeding EUR 4,000,000; annual net turnover excluding tax exceeding EUR 8,000,000; average workforce exceeding 50 employees.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Annual statutory accounts are prepared under French GAAP (Plan Comptable Général, ANC Regulation No. 2018-07). IFRS is not permitted for the individual statutory accounts of an unlisted SARL; IFRS applies only to consolidated accounts of listed groups where required by law.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: France imposes no standalone annual UBO filing. The initial beneficial-owner declaration (déclaration des bénéficiaires effectifs) is filed at incorporation with the trade registry. Any subsequent transfer of shares that changes the direct or indirect ownership of more than 25% of capital or voting rights, or any change in the identity or personal details of a beneficial owner, must be declared to the registry within 30 days of the change. During the annual register audit the manager reviews the share-transfer book; if a reportable transfer has occurred, the amended UBO declaration must be filed before the next applicable registry step. If no change has occurred, no annual UBO renewal fee or filing is due.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members and Share-Transfer Record (Registre des mouvements de titres)
Register of General Meetings and Shareholders' Decisions (Registre des procès-verbaux d'assemblées)
Register of Manager's Decisions and Minutes of Management (Registre des décisions du gérant)

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% standard corporate income tax (IS); reduced 15% rate on the first €42,500 of annual taxable profit for qualifying SMEs (turnover ≤ €10 million and 100% paid-up capital); effective rate for a qualifying small SARL therefore 15% on the initial tranche and 25% on the excess.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Research Tax Credit (CIR) at 30% of eligible R&D expenditure (up to €100 million), Innovation Tax Credit (CII) at 20% for SMEs (capped at €400,000), JEI (Jeune Entreprise Innovante) exemptions, territorial/vitality subsidies, and the preferential 15% SME band; a small novelty-manufacturing SARL realistically uses CII on prototype tooling and die-development expenses but must document the fixed assets directly.
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: No fixed term: French law permits indefinite carryforward; however, annual absorption is statutorily capped at €1,000,000 plus 50% of taxable profit exceeding €1,000,000; an optional one-year carryback (limited to €1,000,000) is available upon election.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 2065-SD (cover sheet of the 'liasse fiscale' 2050-series) with all annexes (2051–2059) filed electronically through the professional tax platform 'impot.gouv.fr' using EFI/EDI (Échange de Formulaires Informatisé) or the EDI declaration service; paper filing is excluded for SARLs above the e-filing requirements.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The annual CIT return is due within three months of the fiscal year-end. For a calendar-year SARL (typical for Etsy merchants), the FY-2024 return must be filed by 3 May 2025 (or the first working day immediately following 1 May); non-calendar year-ends follow the three-month closing rule.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Fiscal-year taxable profit at the standard/reduced rate before loss set-off (Excédent / Bénéfice).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the SARL's entire worldwide-fiscal French taxable income from enamel-pin sales; no owner-level allocation is permitted as the SARL is the sole taxable person.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Fiscal-year loss (Perte) if Etsy/Stripe gross margin is negative after allowable deductions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The loss is recorded for carryforward; it cannot be attributed to the non-resident shareholders or offset outside France.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable result after imputation of prior-year deficits (capped at €1,000,000 plus 50% of the excess).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Verify the prior-year loss schedule (2058-A) is attached before reducing the current-year taxable base.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Prior-year deficits actually imputed against the current-year profit.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only deficits of the French SARL itself may be set off; losses of the ultimate foreign parent are not eligible.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net long-term capital gains eligible for reduced CIT rates (e.g., sale of eligible IP or shares).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the SARL sells its enamel-pin design IP, the reduced rate election must be evidenced in the schedule; no gain exemption for non-resident shareholders at entity level.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Accrued tax credits and prior CIT prepayments (acomptes) to be imputed against the final liability.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Reconcile the four quarterly instalments (forms 2571-SD) and the balance payment (2572-SD) to avoid double assessment.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Allocation of the fiscal result to retained earnings, statutory reserve (5% until 10% of share capital) and distributable dividend pool.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Declared dividends to non-resident shareholders will be processed under Article 119 bis WHT at payment; completeness of this schedule is mandatory for the paying agent.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing: 10% flat surcharge on the assessed CIT. Late payment, and failure to file within 30 days of a formal notice: 40%; fraudulent manoeuvres: 80%; in all cases late-payment interest accrues at 0.20% per month (2.40% annualized). Missing or inaccurate schedules trigger fixed penalties up to €150 per document. Persistent non-filing after formal notice exposes the gérant to criminal referral under Article 1741 CGI.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 2571-SD (advance CIT payments) and form 2572-SD (final balance settlement), both filed via the same EFI/EDI electronic channels on impot.gouv.fr.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Four instalments due 15 March, 15 June, 15 September and 15 December of the current tax year, computed on the previous year's taxable base; the balance (supplément/solde) under form 2572-SD is due on the annual return statutory deadline (3 May for calendar-year SARLs).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Standard-rate and reduced-rate profit pools used to compute the quarterly CIT prepayment.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: No non-resident adjustment; the SARL pays prepayments irrespective of the residence of shareholders.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Difference between total CIT due and quarterly instalments already paid.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Any shortfall attracts 0.20% per-month interest if paid after the statutory deadline.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Non-payment of an instalment: default interest at 0.20% per month and, after notice, the 10% late-payment surcharge; persistent gaps in prepayments trigger immediate collection of remaining instalments and penalties.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 25% final withholding under Article 119 bis-2 CGI on dividends paid by a French SARL to non-resident corporate shareholders; 30% flat withholding (12.8% foreign levy + 17.2% social levies subject to treaty/EEA limitations) for non-resident individuals. The rate is reduced to 0% where the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive applies (10% minimum shareholding held for 24 months) or under an applicable DTA (commonly 0%–15%).
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: The beneficial owner must prove treaty residence by filing a residence certificate (certificat de résidence fiscale) with the French paying SARL before payment date. France issues/accepts certificates on forms 5000 and 5001 series, which the foreign tax authority endorses to certify the owner's residence and beneficial ownership. The payer applies the DTA-reduced or 0% rate at source only when the certificate is in hand; a retroactive refund claim (réclamation contentieuse) can be lodged with the Direction Générale des Finances Publiques if the withholding was over-applied, within the standard limitation period. The SARL, as paying agent, retains the certificate and reports dividend distributions (form 2561) to safeguard its treasury position.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: IP royalties (patents and equivalent industrial/artistic property): 33.33% domestic statutory withholding, generally reduced to 0%–10% under DTAs. Technical-service and commission fees for services rendered in France face a 25% withholding (Article 182 B, as treaty-adjusted). Debt interest: arm's-length interest paid to independent non-resident lenders is exempt from withholding; a 25% (or 75% to non-cooperative states, including ETNC-listed territories) withholding applies to interest paid to related foreign creditors that is disallowed or recharacterized under the thin-capitalization ceiling (maximum debt-to-equity 1.5:1) or routed through tax-haven flow-through entities.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: EUR 50,000,000 (annual net turnover or gross assets of the French entity, or group consolidated turnover) triggers the mandatory Master File and French Local File under Articles L.13 AA/L.13 AB of the Tax Procedure Code; a group Consolidated Revenue threshold of EUR 750,000,000 requires Country-by-Country Reporting. A sub-threshold SARL buying brass blanks, enamel dyes, or design tooling from a related foreign supplier must nonetheless maintain contemporaneous arm's-length evidence, deliverable to the tax authority within 30 days on request.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: France has no UAE-style Economic Substance Regulation filing; substance is enforced through the abuse-of-law doctrine (Article L.64 LPF), the 'acte anormal de gestion' test (any expense must serve the corporation's own commercial interest), the real-seat (siège réel) doctrine, thin-capitalization, and the Principal Purpose Test imported through BEPS MLI treaty clauses. A French SARL producing hard-enamel lapel pins must exhibit genuine operational substance in France: physical premises, employed personnel handling sales and production decisions, ownership of the enamel-pin design IP, and board functions in France. Absent such indicia, the tax administration may recharacterize the SARL as a fiscal conduit and re-attribute the Etsy/Stripe-derived margin to the controlling shareholder abroad.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate under-declaration of Etsy Direct Pay and Stripe revenue, suppression of cash receipts, false VAT/CIT returns, or concealment of foreign payment accounts by the French SARL or its gérant.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Article 1741 CGI: fine up to €500,000 and five years' imprisonment; aggravated cases (use of offshore accounts, organized concealment) raise the exposure to €1,000,000 and seven years. Civil add-ons: 40% concealment/deceit penalty or 80% fraud-penalty on the CIT deficiency, 0.20% monthly interest, €150 per-document penalties, judicial publication, and confirmation of the assessment by the Comité de répression des abus de droit.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The gérant, as legal representative, is personally indictable under Article 1741 and may be sentenced together with the entity: imprisonment, restitution of tax, loss of civic rights, interdiction de gérer, travel bans (interdiction de sortie du territoire), and seizure of personal assets. Veil-piercing tools: Article L.267 LPF allows direct tax recovery against the gérant who fraudulently obstructs collection; in insolvency, the action en comblement de passif (Article L.651-2 of the Commercial Code) holds the gérant civilly liable to the creditors for mismanagement.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: A French SARL with no real staff or premises that books European enamel-pin turnover and strips nearly all margin to a related low-tax Hong Kong or Chinese manufacturing entity through inflated service fees, buy-back commissions, or IP licences, leaving little or no profit in France.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Application of the abuse-of-law procedure (Article L.64 LPF): the arrangement is disregarded, full French CIT/VAT is re-established on the economic substance, and an 80% deliberate-abuse penalty plus 0.20% monthly interest is applied. Denied-deduction treatment under the acte anormal de gestion rule re-adds the inflated expenses for a 25% to 40% correction; the administration may also lift the filing burden of proof against the taxpayer.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The gérant who engineered the shell structure risks criminal complicity in tax evasion, personal recharacterization of the tax debt under Article L.267 LPF, a ban on directing commercial companies for up to 15 years, travel restrictions, and civil restitution orders in liquidation proceedings.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Non-arm's-length cross-border purchases of die-struck brass blanks, enamel pigments, or assembly services from a related supplier; payment of excessive interest/royalties to the foreign parent; and failure to produce the Local File or supporting comparables on request, especially where French burden-of-proof rules are reversed.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Transfer-pricing adjustment re-adding the excess to French taxable profit, plus a 40% intentional misdeclaration penalty and 0.20% monthly interest; interest deduction disallowance under the 1.5:1 thin-cap ratio; a 25% withholding (75% to ETNC jurisdictions) is reinstated on the recharacterized interest and royalty flows; non-production of documentation reverses the burden of proof and can trigger the deliberative penalty without the administration needing to prove a wrong price.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The gérant signing the returns and approving the intercompany pricing is personally exposed to criminal administrative concealment penalties, civil recovery of the unpaid tax via clawback actions, and professional disqualification where the pricing scheme was deliberately used to drain French profits.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Acceptance of cash above the statutory ceilings (€1,000 for French-resident consumers and professionals; €10,000 for non-resident tourists), non-registration of the beneficiary-owner declaration (Déclaration des Bénéficiaires Effectifs), or funneling Etsy/Stripe funds through unregistered accounts to obscure the beneficial owner and avoid Tracfin reporting.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Cash-limit breaches: contraventional fines up to €15,000 and disallowance of the unbanked expense for tax purposes; DBE omissions: fine up to €7,500 for natural persons and €37,500 for the SARL, plus possible imprisonment for deliberate concealment of the effective owner; undeclared foreign accounts: €1,500 fixed penalty per account (up to €10,000 per account in non-cooperative states) under Article 1729-0 A and the presumption that the hidden balance constitutes taxable income.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The gérant who personally disposes of hidden accounts or signs the DBE containing false beneficial owners incurs criminal liability for money-laundering declarations (Article L.561-3 of the Monetary and Financial Code), a ban on management, confiscation of the sums, and personal enforcement for the corporate penalties under the fraudulent-obstruction rule.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Undisclosed Foreign Payment Rails and Digital-Sales Omission
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Use of Etsy Direct Pay or Stripe funds held in US/IRL settlement accounts without declaring the account(s) on form 3916/3916-bis, or failure to integrate marketplace settlement reports into the CIT liasse, thus permanently erasing taxable marketplace turnover.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Withholding the foreign-account declaration triggers the €1,500/account penalty and the statutory presumption that the funds are unreported taxable income; digital-sales concealment further attracts the 40%-80% penalties and late-payment interest on the omitted CIT base; the tax authority may also apply the 10% late-filing surcharge and seize settlement funds from Etsy/Stripe through third-party attachment.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The gérant is criminally and civilly exposed when settlement accounts are under the gérant's private name while economically belonging to the SARL; courts may treat the structure as fraudulent concealment, triggering imprisonment, personal recoupment of tax, and a travel ban pending full restitution.
